title: Pin-bound mini-cohort rollouts and gated split experiments for model revisions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context: We need a safe, observable way to validate new model revisions that are pinned by customers before broad promotion. Current pin behavior applies a single model revision to a customer pin; there is no built-in ability to run small controlled cohorts, shadow runs, or split-sample experiments bounded by the pin. This blocks faster adoption of improved revisions and makes rollbacks manual and risky.

Objective: Deliver a pin-aware deployment pattern that supports:
- Mini-cohort rollouts (1%/5%/20%) restricted to a single pin boundary.
- Synchronized shadow and split evaluation paths for quality and latency comparison without affecting production responses except for optional canary routing.
- Automatic telemetry gates (latency, token-cost, regression on prompt testsets) that can pause or rollback traffic for that pin.
- Simple A/B-style experiments scoped to a pin with result export to the evals pipeline and Redwood Console dashboards.

Acceptance criteria:
1) API: Pin config supports an opt-in field "cohort_config" allowing percentages, evaluation prompt set, and rollback thresholds. Documented in the API spec.
2) Routing: Requests for pinned customers can be deterministically routed to the control or candidate group while preserving KV cache isolation and SLO exposure accounting.
3) Telemetry: Console shows per-pin split metrics (latency P50/P95, token cost, eval-quality deltas) and raises an alert when thresholds are breached.
4) Safety: Shadow evaluation runs have no side effects; fallback path must exist and be automatic on threshold breach.
5) Evals integration: Candidate outputs are logged to the evals pipeline with linkage to the pin + cohort ID.

Scope:
In scope: API surface for pin-cohort config, routing layer changes to support deterministic split per-pin, metric tagging and Console dashboard updates, integration with existing evals ingestion.
Out of scope: UI-sidepin management flows for pin creation (handled by separate UX work), enterprise policy & RBAC granularity for who can create cohorts (follow-up).

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Deterministic split vs random: We chose hash-based deterministic assignment using customer identifier + cohort salt to avoid traffic drift during server restarts.
- KV cache isolation: To avoid cross-cohort contamination, we replicate KV cache namespaces per cohort for pinned customers; this increases memory usage per model instance but keeps quality comparisons clean.
- Telemetry gating sensitivity: Conservative default thresholds to reduce false positives; customers can tighten thresholds per pin.

Dependencies:
- ENG-2987 (staged safety heuristics) for integration points with safety checks.
- ENG-4120 (telemetry tagging pipeline) for new metric dimensions.

Artifacts & links:
- Owner spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/ModelOnboard/PinCohortSpec
- Draft API PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-api/pull/7342
- Routing prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/compare/pin-cohort-routing
- Eval ingestion dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/pin-cohort-evals

Operational runbook:
- How to start a cohort: POST /pins/{pin_id}/cohorts with cohort_config (see spec).
- Emergency stop: release endpoint to set cohort percentage to 0; automatic when telemetry gate trips.
- Postmortem triggers: any rollout that trips gating will create a postmortem ticket and snapshot model outputs for 24 hours.

Risks & mitigation:
- Memory blowup from per-cohort KV caches: mitigate by enforcing a max concurrent cohorts per model (default 3) and eviction policy.
- False regressions from small sample sizes: require minimum sample count before gating decisions.
- Customer confusion about pin semantics: add Console explainer and default-off cohort for pins created pre-feature rollout.
